parts.article:
The Peopling of Patagonia
 
Anthropologists continue to investigate human migration to Patagonia at the southern tip of South America
 
(A) The human settlement of the southern extremity of the Americas has always fascinated prehistorians. Viewed from a global perspective, this was the last major continental land mass to be reached by human beings. The earliest occupation of Patagonia carries obvious implications for understanding when the North and South American continents were peopled, because it gives a baseline that all calculations regarding the rate of dispersion of humans throughout both continents must take into account.
 
(B) For many years the human settlement of North and South America has been conceived of as beginning in the far north and travelling progressively southwards to Patagonia. However, fundamental disagreements developed concerning the length of time involved. Some scholars accepted a human presence in the Americas as early as 20,000 years ago, while others proposed that it could date no earlier than 8,000 years ago, and the debate is still with us today.
 
(C) The idea of a relatively ‘late’ settlement of the Americas (around 8,000 years ago) implies that a rapid process of migration took place. Herein lies a second debate, which revolves around the question of how migration is to be understood. The ‘late’ model demands a hypothetical migration conceived of as a single, continually advancing wave of settlement. This has always been difficult to take seriously, and many scholars now support the idea of an ‘early’ model that sees the migration as a less ordered migration, and this is surely the most realistic scenario as migrants slowly adapted to the diverse natural habitats they would have met while travelling through the continent.
 
(D) Those who argue for an earlier settlement, however, must contend with the lack of unequivocal evidence for archaeological sites older than around 14,000 years. Nevertheless, evidence for human occupation of the centre of South America is now securely dated to around 12,500 years ago at the Monte Verde site, which casts doubt on the ‘late’ model. The lack of archaeological evidence further south for this time period may be explained by the obstacle to humans on foot posed by the huge glacial streams that were present at that time.
 
(E) We can speculate then that the retreat of the Patagonian glaciers around 14,000 years ago allowed the initial human intrusion into a pristine environment, which was similar to that of early post-glacial Europe. Human settlement of the vast horizontal expanse of treeless high country must have been tenuous at best, and the evidence for this occupation remains relatively scant, most of it coming from rock shelters in Argentina and Chile. There is, however, reliable evidence from these sites to confirm the presence of humans by around 11,000 years ago in different habitats, and some hints of an even older occupation. However, some other sites where evidence for even earlier human occupation was initially posited have recently come under fresh scrutiny. This is because anthropologists have come to recognise that bones or other evidence may be deposited in caves by natural agency—in other words, by other forces such as floods or predators—and not necessarily by humans.
 
(F) We shall turn now to a more detailed discussion of the archaeological evidence found in various parts of Patagonia. At the site located beside Chinchihuapi Creek, excavations have produced convincing evidence of human occupation, including hut foundations and wooden artefacts. They were buried in layers of peat, which has the property of preserving wood remarkably well, and as a result, radiocarbon dating tests have shown these artefacts to date from around 12,500 years ago. One of the most famous Patagonian sites is a cave known as Los Toldos. However, the evidence from this site has recently been called into question, because dispersed flecks of carbon used in the test process were taken unsystematically from many different places at the site. As a result, the association of this material with the artefacts is not at all clear. About 150 kilometres to the south is the site called El Ceibo, where a similar collection of artefacts to that found at Los Toldos has been discovered from the lowest levels of the dig, but as yet no radiocarbon dates are available, and this sort of analysis of the existing evidence is required before the site’s value can be confirmed.
 
(G) The Arroyo Eeo site is located very close to the high plateau. The artefacts from the earliest occupations were found at the same depth and have the same origins as those from Los Toldos, and have been securely dated to around 9,000 years ago. Another site that is mentioned in the debate is at Las Buitreras, where a number of stone flakes associated with bone remains of various animals have been discovered. However, anthropologists now believe that presumed cut marks on the bones are somewhat dubious, and despite detailed testing there is no way of securely relating any of these remains to human occupation. Finally, some 50 kilometres to the south is the site at Cueva Fell, which was the first Patagonian site to be systematically studied by modern archaeological methods. However, it is now recognised that the utility of this site must be restricted to its direct vicinity, given changes to the nearby area caused by flooding, and findings cannot be freely extrapolated further afield.
 
(H) In conclusion, based on the evidence from a number of reliable sites, it seems probable that human populations reached Patagonia around 11,000 years ago.
parts.questions:
Questions 27–31
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 27–31 on your answer sheet.

Q27 In the first paragraph, what is the writer’s main point about migration to Patagonia?

  • A It started earlier than previously thought.
  • B Historians have overlooked its importance.
  • C It impacts on research into the wider region.
  • D Researchers have calculated its effects on the environment.

Q28 In the second paragraph, what is the writer’s purpose?

  • A to challenge previous research
  • B to propose new areas to investigate
  • C to summarise a scholarly debate
  • D to suggest reasons for human migration

Q29 The writer refers to the ‘late’ model in order to

  • A compare it with another theory of migration.
  • B evaluate the success of American migration.
  • C criticise the speed of research into migration.
  • D compare migration in different parts of the world.

Q30 What is the writer’s main point about the ‘early’ model?

  • A Scholars support the idea of fast migrations.
  • B It is too random to be a convincing theory.
  • C South America was more habitable at an earlier time.
  • D It is more consistent with the physical conditions of the land.

Q31 What does the writer suggest about the Monte Verde site?

  • A It is much younger than researchers once estimated.
  • B It provides supporting evidence for relatively early settlement.
  • C Archaeologists believe the site is of questionable value.
  • D Streams exposed the site, making new research possible.

Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 32–35 on your answer sheet, write:

Q32 The conditions encountered by the first migrants to Patagonia were unique.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q33 In the high country the first migrants hunted wild animals for food.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q34 Archaeologists have failed to draw conclusions from the evidence found at rock shelters in Argentina and Chile.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q35 Archaeological evidence can be moved from place to place in a variety of ways.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN
Questions 36–40

Write the correct letter, A-J, in boxes 36–40 on your answer sheet.
The archaeological evidence from Patagonia
Building remains and other evidence have been found in at the Chinchihuapi Creek site, and because of this it has been possible to date them to around 12,500 years ago. However, the of the samples taken from Los Toldos means that this site is of doubtful value. El Ceibo is a more promising dig, where the examination of artefacts would be beneficial in order to confirm the usefulness of discoveries there. The remains found at the Arroyo Eeo site show and date from around 9,000 years ago. Unfortunately, no can be made between the samples taken from Las Buitreras and human presence. The findings of the work carried out at Cueva Fell cannot provide useful information beyond the . In conclusion, though the evidence is mixed, it is believed that the human population of Patagonia began about 11,000 years ago.

Q27

干扰 你可能被“earliest”迷惑选 A，但作者强调的是这个地点对“研究更广泛地区（wider region）”的参考价值。

句子 (A段) The earliest occupation of Patagonia carries obvious implications for understanding when the North and South American continents were peopled, because it gives a baseline that all calculations regarding the rate of dispersion of humans throughout both continents must take into account.

解析 第一段提到巴塔哥尼亚的定居为理解整个南北美洲的人类扩散率提供了一个基准线（baseline）。

Q28

解析 第二段总结了关于人类何时到达美洲的不同学术观点，即 20,000 年还是 8,000 年前的争论。

干扰 作者只是陈述了目前存在的不同观点（debate），并没有偏袒某一方或提出新领域。

句子 (B段) However, fundamental disagreements developed concerning the length of time involved. Some scholars accepted... while others proposed... and the debate is still with us today.

Q29

解析 文中通过对比“晚期模型”的一波流迁移和“早期模型”的缓慢适应过程，来探讨迁移是如何进行的。

干扰 “late”模型的出现是为了引出与其对立的“early”模型，从而讨论迁移的模式（单次浪潮 vs 缓慢适应）。

句子 (C段) The ‘late’ model demands a hypothetical migration conceived of as a single, continually advancing wave of settlement. ...many scholars now support the idea of an ‘early’ model that sees the migration as a less ordered migration...

Q30

句子 (C段) ...and this is surely the most realistic scenario as migrants slowly adapted to the diverse natural habitats they would have met while travelling through the continent.

解析 “早期模型”认为迁移是缓慢且不断适应各种自然栖息地的，作者认为这比“一波流”更符合实际（realistic）。

干扰 这里的“physical conditions”对应原文中的“diverse natural habitats”，强调人类是随着环境变化而缓慢移动的。

Q31

解析 Monte Verde 遗址的时间被确定在 12,500 年前，这有力地支持了早于 8,000 年的“早期定居”理论。

干扰 虽然 D 段提到了溪流（streams），但那是解释为什么南方缺乏证据的原因，而不是说溪流暴露了遗址。

句子 (D段) Nevertheless, evidence for human occupation of the centre of South America is now securely dated to around 12,500 years ago at the Monte Verde site, which casts doubt on the ‘late’ model.

Q32

解析 原文说巴塔哥尼亚的环境与早期的欧洲后期冰川环境“相似（similar）”，所以并非“独特（unique）”。

干扰 “Unique”意味着独一无二，这与原文的“similar”直接发生矛盾。

句子 (E段) ...allowed the initial human intrusion into a pristine environment, which was similar to that of early post-glacial Europe.

Q33

解析 文章提到了高地（high country）和动物骨头，但并未提及第一批移民是否在那“狩猎野生动物获取食物”。

干扰 看到“bone remains”不要脑补狩猎行为，原文只讨论了骨头上的痕迹是否为人类造成，未提及狩猎。

句子 (E段) Human settlement of the vast horizontal expanse of treeless high country must have been tenuous at best... (G段) ...a number of stone flakes associated with bone remains of various animals have been discovered.

Q34

干扰 题目说“未能得出结论（failed to draw conclusions）”，而原文说有“可靠证据确认存在（reliable evidence... to confirm）”。

句子 (E段) There is, however, reliable evidence from these sites to confirm the presence of humans by around 11,000 years ago in different habitats...

解析 考古学家通过这些岩穴遗址得出了结论，确认了大约 11,000 年前人类的存在。

Q35

解析 文中明确提到洪水或捕食者等自然力量（natural agency）会将骨头等证据移动到洞穴中。

干扰 “Moved from place to place” 对应原文的 “deposited in caves by natural agency”。

句子 (E段) This is because anthropologists have come to recognise that bones or other evidence may be deposited in caves by natural agency—in other words, by other forces such as floods or predators—and not necessarily by humans.

Q36

解析 泥炭（peat）具有非常好的保存特性，使得木制品处于良好的保存状态。

干扰 原文用的是“preserving wood remarkably well”，对应选项中的“good condition”。

句子 (F段) They were buried in layers of peat, which has the property of preserving wood remarkably well...

Q37

句子 (F段) ...because dispersed flecks of carbon used in the test process were taken unsystematically from many different places at the site.

解析 Los Toldos 的样本采集是“非系统性的（unsystematically）”，即随机采集的，导致价值存疑。

干扰 “Unsystematically” 完美对应选项 B “random”。

Q38

解析 Arroyo Eeo 发现的器物与 Los Toldos 的器物深度相同、起源相同，即具有相似的特征。

干扰 原文提到“same origins”和“same depth”，指向这些物件具有“相似的属性”。

句子 (G段) The artefacts from the earliest occupations were found at the same depth and have the same origins as those from Los Toldos...

Q39

解析 在 Las Buitreras，无法将动物残骸与人类活动可靠地联系起来。

干扰 原文说“no way of securely relating”，对应选项 H 的“no reliable connection”。

句子 (G段) ...and despite detailed testing there is no way of securely relating any of these remains to human occupation.

Q40

解析 洪水改变了周边环境，因此 Cueva Fell 的发现只能局限于其直接邻近区域，不能外推。

干扰 “Direct vicinity” 直接对应选项 J 的 “immediate surroundings”。

句子 (G段) However, it is now recognised that the utility of this site must be restricted to its direct vicinity, given changes to the nearby area caused by flooding, and findings cannot be freely extrapolated further afield.
